chapter_summary: Defines the spike-and-channel trend: a spike (one or more trend bars with little overlap, or a large gap), a pullback of one to a dozen bars, then a lower-momentum channel that ends at a measured move or third push, breaks against the trend, and corrects to the channel start where a double bottom forms and a 25 percent bounce follows. Produced the spike/trend-bar/overlap/doji primitives and a spike state machine, spike-close and pullback-resumption entries, spike-bottom stop, measured-move exits (spike height, leg1=leg2, measuring gap), channel entries (below prior low, EMA/trend-line pullbacks, MA gap bar), channel-strength filters (tightness, opposite bodies, overlap, dojis), consecutive-climax detector with exits and blocking filters, opposite-spike/trading-range filters, opening-range and gap-day intraday filters, and a set of reversal setups (wedge overshoot, three pushes, double bottom at channel start, failed breakouts, second entry). Most of the second half is chart discussion; primitives from the first half are reused throughout. Chapter 22 and the Part IV intro define the same opening-range primitives.
